meta.description: How to report a vulnerability in our website, what is in scope and what you can expect from us.

security.title: Responsible disclosure policy
security.intro: If you have found a vulnerability in our website, we want to know. This policy explains how to report it and what you can expect from us.

draft.title: Commitments pending confirmation
draft.body: The timelines, the safe harbor and the other commitments in this policy are a proposal. Confirm them with the company and with legal counsel before publishing.

blocks.text: Write to us at [{securityEmail}](mailto:{securityEmail}) with a clear description of the problem, the steps to reproduce it and its potential impact.
You can also check our [security.txt](/.well-known/security.txt) file, which follows the RFC 9116 standard.
[COMPLETE: if you have a PGP key, state its fingerprint here and where to download it]
The {legalName} website and its subdomains are in scope. The following are out of scope:

items: Third-party services we use (hosting, email, database…). Report those to the relevant provider.
Social engineering, phishing or physical access against our staff or premises.
Automated reports without a proof of concept or a demonstrable impact.
Low-risk findings without an exploitable impact, such as a missing header that does not amount to a real vulnerability.
Act in good faith and avoid affecting other people, their data or the availability of the service.
Access only what is strictly necessary to demonstrate the problem, and do not keep or share personal data.
Do not modify or delete data.
Give us a reasonable amount of time to fix the problem before making it public.

sections.title: What you can expect from us

items: We will acknowledge receipt of your report within a target of 3 business days.
We will assess the finding and keep you informed of progress.
We will fix confirmed issues, prioritized by severity.
With your permission, we will publicly acknowledge your contribution.

blocks.text: [COMPLETE: confirm the response times the company can commit to]
We will not take legal action against people who report vulnerabilities in good faith and comply with this policy. [COMPLETE: review this statement with legal counsel]
We do not currently offer monetary rewards (a bug bounty). We appreciate every report and, if you wish, we will acknowledge you publicly.
